identification.summary: UTA0355 is Volexity's designation for a Russia-linked cluster that runs targeted social-engineering campaigns against people and organizations connected to Ukraine and European security policy, with the goal of obtaining access to Microsoft 365 accounts [S1][S3]. The actor makes contact by email with a video-conference invitation, follows up over Signal or WhatsApp to add legitimacy, and steers the victim to a Microsoft 365 login and OAuth or device-code workflow [S1][S3]. Volexity assesses with high confidence that UTA0355 registered devices and downloaded email data from compromised accounts [S1]. Volexity first described it in April 2025 alongside a second cluster, UTA0352 [S1][S4], and described further activity in December 2025 that spoofed European security conferences [S2][S5].
identification.firstObserved: Described publicly by Volexity on 2025-04-22 [S1][S4]; the earliest underlying activity date is not stated in the sources gathered.
identification.notes: UTA0355 is a Volexity 'UTA' (unattributed threat actor) cluster name, not a Microsoft name; no Microsoft mapping was found. UTA0352 is a separate Volexity cluster covered in the same April 2025 report and must not be merged with UTA0355 [S1][S4]. Secondary coverage says the April 2025 report did not link either cluster to known Russian APT groups, though it noted overlaps with other actors seeking Microsoft 365 access [S4]. Microsoft's separate reporting on Void Blizzard posing as a defense summit organizer is a different cluster and is not merged here [S5].

attribution.confidence: Coverage of the April 2025 report states Volexity assesses the clusters are Russian with medium confidence [S3][S4]. Volexity's later report is described as tracking UTA0355 as Russia-linked [S2][S5]. No government attribution to a specific Russian service was found.
attribution.basis: Volexity assessment based on targeting of Ukraine-related persons and the social-engineering themes, as reported by secondary outlets [S3][S4]. The primary Volexity text could not be opened, so the exact evidentiary basis is unverified [S1].

objectives: Access to Microsoft 365 mailboxes and data of Ukraine-linked NGOs, think tanks and individuals, and later of attendees of European security events, via stolen OAuth authorization codes and registered devices, consistent with intelligence collection from email [S1][S2][S3].

sectors: Human rights and Ukraine-focused advocacy individuals
Government and security policy community (attendees of European security events)
regions: Europe (security conference lures such as the Belgrade Security Conference) [S5]
targeting.notes: April 2025 coverage describes targets as NGOs, think tanks and individuals with Ukraine connections [S3][S4]. December 2025 coverage describes lures impersonating the Belgrade Security Conference [S5]. Victim counts are not given in the sources gathered.

capabilities.summary: Patient, one-to-one social engineering across email, Signal and WhatsApp, with impersonation of European officials or event organizers [S3][S5]. Technique centers on Microsoft 365 OAuth and device-code workflows: the victim is sent to a legitimate Microsoft login and then asked to return a code or the full browser URL containing an OAuth authorization code [S1][S5]. In one reported variant the actor sent lures from a compromised Ukrainian government email account [S3]. After obtaining the code the actor registered a new device in Entra ID, social-engineered a 2FA approval and downloaded email data [S1][S3]. Later access to compromised accounts was reported to run through proxy-network nodes, and the rogue device was reported to be named like the victim's real device [S2]. Malware use was not reported in the sources gathered.

campaigns.name: Video-call lures against Ukraine-linked NGOs (Volexity 'Phishing for Codes')
campaigns.summary: Volexity reported UTA0355 emailing video-conference invitations, moving to Signal or WhatsApp, directing victims to a Microsoft 365 login and seeking a 2FA approval to register devices and download email. One variant used a compromised Ukrainian government account [S1][S3][S4].

campaigns.name: Spoofed European security conference lures (Volexity 'Dangerous Invitations')
campaigns.summary: Volexity described fake event sites and WhatsApp or Signal 'live support' used to get victims to complete a Microsoft 365 device-code or OAuth sign-up, with contact often starting weeks earlier. A named lure was the Belgrade Security Conference [S2][S5].

diamond.adversary: Russia-linked cluster tracked by Volexity as UTA0355, assessed Russian with medium confidence per coverage; sponsor not identified [S3][S4].
diamond.capability: Social engineering over email, Signal and WhatsApp; Microsoft 365 OAuth and device-code abuse; Entra ID device registration; email download [S1][S5].
diamond.infrastructure: Fake event sites, a compromised Ukrainian government email account in one variant, and proxy-network nodes for later account access [S2][S3].
diamond.victim: Ukraine-linked NGOs, think tanks and individuals; attendees of European security events [S3][S5].
diamond.socioPolitical: Collection on Ukraine-related policy and European security discussions during the war in Ukraine [S3][S5].
diamond.technology: Microsoft 365 / Entra ID tenants lacking device-based conditional access, and users who can be talked into returning OAuth codes or URLs; end-user messaging apps used for trust building [S1][S3].

gaps: Volexity's primary reports (April 2025 and December 2025) could not be opened in this session (host unreachable); all details come from secondary coverage and search summaries [S1][S2].
The 'medium confidence' Russian attribution wording was taken from search summaries of secondary coverage and should be checked against the Volexity text [S3][S4].
Specific Russian service or sponsor is unknown; no government attribution found.
Exact earliest activity date, victim counts and full indicator lists (IPs, domains, client IDs) were not verified.
Relationship to other Russian device-code phishing clusters (for example Microsoft-tracked actors) is not established in the sources gathered; do not merge.
Publication dates for the secondary articles are given to month precision only.

A source was removed because its URL did not appear in fact-check searches; lookalike-domain and Brussels Indo-Pacific Dialogue lure details that rested only on it were deleted. The Volexity URLs (S1, S2) were not seen verbatim in search results although their titles were corroborated.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is the Microsoft 365 / Entra ID tenant and the personal messaging accounts of staff who support Ukraine or European security engagement; conferences and working-group calls are the pretext surface [S1][S5]. STEP 2: The actor exploits identity workflows rather than software flaws, so standard patching does not close the gap; patience and rapport are its edge [S5]. STEP 3: Template is email invitation, then Signal or WhatsApp rapport, then OAuth or device-code login, then registered device and mailbox download [S1][S3]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued targeting of Ukraine-linked and security-policy individuals using event and meeting lures. MDCOA is use of a compromised government or partner mailbox to lure DoD, coalition or contractor personnel, leading to mailbox collection of planning correspondence. Candidate indicators: unexpected newly registered Entra devices, device names mimicking the user's own, OAuth sign-ins from proxy-network IPs, unsolicited meeting invitations followed by requests to return a URL or code [S1][S2][S5].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: feed Entra ID sign-in and device-registration logs into watch-floor monitoring and brief personnel on unsolicited meeting invitations from partner nations [S1][S2]. (2) Authorities: conditional-access changes and blocking of device-code flow fall to the tenant owner, so confirm who may direct them across the DODIN segment involved [S1]. (3) Mission assurance: personal-device messaging contact with adversary-operated personas bypasses enterprise controls; include it in force protection and user-awareness guidance [S3][S5]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with mission partners and report suspected compromise of partner or government mailboxes through established channels [S3].

provenance.importedSummary: UTA0355 is a Russian threat actor that conducts phishing campaigns targeting individuals and organizations associated with Ukraine. The actor initiates contact via email, inviting targets to a video conference, and follows up through Signal or WhatsApp to enhance legitimacy. After establishing communication, UTA0355 prompts victims to log in via a malicious M365 URL, subsequently requesting approval for a 2FA authentication to access email data. Volexity assesses with high confidence that UTA0355 successfully registered devices and downloaded email data from compromised accounts.
